title: THE KING's fight: the aggro on the mechs and the hull, the 40 mm that stops and turns it, the called nuke
context: Owner, 2026-11-12 night: "The Arena; all the elements should be there already; we tune the aggro of the King so that it aims for the mechs and the tank, the player controls the gunship, and needs to time the shells so they a) do not deal friendly fire damage and b) stop the King in its track and funnels it to a spot where a nuke is about to drop." Earlier the same day: "the mechs should be more tactical too, and the desired state is that the player in the gunship has agency doing two actions a) barrage smaller shells to protect friendlies and b) time it for a great nuke." The owner asleep; the agent's calls are in docs/DECISIONS.md "The arena fight (2026-11-12 night), for the owner's review". Branch arena-king from 5c6d3b52, unpushed. Found first: the 2026-10-23 diagnosis (the boss a cell-graph walker puppeteering the kit) no longer held; since arena-lab-fight her body owns her position and runs the lab's fear and temperament, so the fight was built on that engine.
outcome: BUILT in four stages, each committed green. (1) src/domain/king-fight.js (pure, test/king-fight.mjs) and ARENA_KING (src/content/arena-king.js): the King hunts the hull or a standing Ridgeback within 140 m (nearest; a mech that hit it in the last 4 s, or the hull as the bait, worth 40 m; held 6 s), stalks 45 m short, tells 1.5 s (it holds with its arms long toward the target, red rings under the target and under it, a callout), charges the locked point at chase speed 4 for at most 2.5 s, hits what is within 22 m once (a hull dent, 5 of a mech's 12 points), recovers 2.5 s. The record wears armour 0.1 (src/fx/creature-enemies.js damageScale). The Ridgebacks have points, go down for the run at 0 (on their side, guns out of towers()), fall back at 0.4 cells/s from a tell or charge on them and spread on the King's ring (src/fx/mech-squad.js, src/domain/mech-roles.js fleeStep). A 40 mm near the body staggers it 1.2 s with diminishing returns (x0.5, none under 0.25 s, recovering 0.35 a second) and veers it 30 m away from the burst for 2.5 s, in place of the lab's wild flight (src/fx/boss/arena-fight.js with `king`; without it the lab's behaviour is unchanged). (2) The player's rounds in the boss phase hurt the hull and the mechs within their blast (ARENA_KING.friendly, once per unit per gun every 1.5 s / 3 s). (3) The MK-9 is called: the first press marks the cell (src/domain/gunship.js heavyPaintAt), the round is let go so it lands 8 s after the mark, with any gun in hand (src/sentry-pilot.js releaseHeavy; a bug where only a selected MK-9 released it was found by --king and fixed), no second press, re-mark or nudge; on the King (centre within the blast + 10 m) 30 % of 180 unscaled by the armour, a miss nothing; a mech in its blast 8 points, the hull two dents; the mechs walk out of the marker. (4) Readouts: the strip's THE KING row and the MK-9 · IMPACT countdown row (a `clock` row: seconds, never worn), the seat's MARKED · IMPACT IN n S, the mark painted in the optic for the countdown and pulsed on the ground, THE KING card's two actions and this fight's controls (src/fx/choice-card.js: a hint of several lines).
alternatives: Isao announces the nuke's spot: rejected, the player's choice of the spot is the owner's 'time it for a great nuke'.
A limited stock of nukes (three or four a fight): not taken; a miss costs the 8 s countdown and the 6 s reload, about 14 s.
The lab's wild flight for the 40 mm (a 35 m erratic run): replaced in this fight, its erratic course cannot herd.
A downed Ridgeback standing up after the fight: not taken, the loss is the cost of a careless nuke or shell.
The King hunting the nearest unit alone, or the most recent attacker alone: the batteries never stop firing, so attacker-first always picked a mech.
evidence: scripts/browser-lock.sh node scripts/browser-test.mjs --king (from a snapshot of the tree): PASS 4 (king-card, king-tell, king-marker, king-end). With harness hands: the first tell 19 s after the seat (on the hull); a 40 mm 10 m off staggered it and it moved 9.7 m away from the burst; a 40 mm on a Ridgeback took 1.5 of its 12 points (three mechs stood in the burst at the drop); three marked nukes landed 31.6, 2.9 and 11.3 m from its centre, 54 points each; dead at 74.6 s of game clock from the seat (116 s of wall); its points: nukes 162, everything else 17.8; its targets over the fight hull, m3, m1, m0; 7 tells, 6 charges (3 reached mechs, none the hull), 9 staggers, 18 veers; two Ridgebacks downed by the harness's own nukes, no hull lost.

Second --king run on the final tree (the mark painted in the optic): PASS 4 (king-card, king-tell, king-marker, king-end); dead at 80.3 s of game clock (117 s of wall); three nukes 11.1, 10.1 and 52.6 m off, 54 points each, everything else 17.2 (a fourth mark went down on 1 point); targets hull, m0, m3; 6 tells, 5 charges, none reaching a unit; a 40 mm 10 m off: stopped, 8.9 m away from the burst; no Ridgeback and no hull lost. The marker screenshot shows the blast ring in the thermal optic round the King, the red ring in GROUND TRUTH and MK-9 · IMPACT 5 S on the strip.

The first --king run (before the release fix): the mark never released with the 25 mm in hand; the harness's 580 herding shells alone killed it in 771 s of game clock (the armour holds the shells to a minor share per round).
--arena PASS 6 on stage 1 (its card title assertion corrected to THE KING, the title since 7be0f7ed).
npm test: 345 test programs passed; npm run check green at every commit (td-tab 5352 lines under 5450, no long line).
